aubergine-ink.$description: Aubergine Ink — Primary text, heading borders, and brand character — the slight warm-purple undertone replaces conventional near-black, giving Duna a distinctive almost-black that is neither pure black nor navy

espresso.$description: Espresso — Primary action fill — filled buttons (Get started, Schedule a demo). Slightly warmer and darker than Aubergine Ink, used exclusively for interactive surfaces that need to feel pressed-into the page

warm-ash.$description: Warm Ash — Muted secondary text and subtle borders — a desaturated warm gray that softens long-form copy without competing with the primary text

graphite.$description: Graphite — Body text variant, icon strokes, input borders — the workhorse neutral for non-heading content

stone.$description: Stone — Tertiary text and dividers — a lighter warm gray for labels, metadata, and less important copy

onyx.$description: Onyx — Icon fills and select text instances — the deepest near-black in the scale, reserved for graphic emphasis

smoke.$description: Smoke — Icon borders, card edge cases, and dark UI elements — a warm-tinted dark for graphical components

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Heading borders and dark decorative fills — a warm brown-black for borders on headings and subtle structural elements

paper-white.$description: Paper White — Primary surface — cards, buttons, and the dominant page background

linen.$description: Linen — Warm canvas background — the off-white page tint that gives the entire system its warm, paper-like atmosphere instead of clinical pure white

bone.$description: Bone — Card surfaces and subtle elevated panels — a barely-warm cream for cards sitting on the Linen canvas

mist.$description: Mist — Input field background — the only functional surface tint that signals a fillable area

sans-serif.$description: sans-serif — detected in extracted data but not described by AI

gt-america.$description: Primary typeface across all UI — body at 400, emphasis at 500, display at 400 with aggressive negative tracking. The compressed, geometric forms at large sizes give headlines an editorial, almost legal-document authority rather than the typical rounded SaaS friendliness.

gt-america-regular.$description: GT America Regular — detected in extracted data but not described by AI
